_meta.document: District Environment Plan for Chikkaballapura District, Karnataka (2021)
_meta.note_image_only: Scanned/image-only PDF; pdftotext and pypdf return zero text. Extracted via pdftoppm + tesseract OCR, then every final figure visually verified against the rendered page image at 250dpi.
_meta.page_offset: Printed page label = PDF page number - 1 (cover is unnumbered). Citations below give both.

hazardous_waste.facility_status: No TSDF, no SLF, no standalone incinerators in the district. Integrated Transport Storage Disposal Facility (TSDF): Nil; Sanitary Landfill Facility (SLF): Nil; Standalone incinerators: Nil. HW generated by industry is disposed through authorized off-district TSDFs, incinerators and recyclers via MoU, monitored by KSPCB. One used-oil recycling industry in district: M/s Lakshmi Refinerries, Gowribidanur. No contaminated or probable-contaminated sites.
hazardous_waste.page: PDF p.73 (printed p.72), continuing PDF p.74-75 (printed p.73-74)
hazardous_waste.notes: All five core figures visually confirmed on PDF p.73. Internal consistency check passes: 143.90 + 194.29 + 60.63 = 398.82 MT/Annum exactly. All 38 industries authorized by KSPCB and monitored by RO KSPCB.

bmw_generated_per_day_alt.source_page: PDF p.69 (printed p.68) gaps/adequacy table; see caveat

biomedical_waste.facility_status: 2 Common Biomedical Waste Treatment & Disposal Facilities (CBWTFs/CBMWTFs) serve the district. (1) M/s Prajwal BMW Management System, Gowribidanur, Chikkaballapura (D) [in-district] - Incinerator 200 Kg/hr, Autoclave 400 litres/cycle. (2) M/s Meera Envirotech Pvt. Ltd., Kolar [out-of-district, within 75 km] - Incinerator 100 Kg/hr, Autoclave 350 ltrs. No deep burial pits in Govt HCFs. 100% of generated BMW is treated. Covid waste handed to both CBMWTFs.
biomedical_waste.page: PDF p.67 (printed p.66) inventory table; gaps narrative PDF p.68-72 (printed p.67-71)
biomedical_waste.notes: Inventory table (PDF p.67) figures all visually confirmed. The document is internally inconsistent on the daily BMW tonnage: the inventory table (PDF p.67) says 378.221 kg/day generated AND treated; a later adequacy table (PDF p.69, visually confirmed) says 378.58 kg/day generated AND disposed against 578 existing HCFs. Both values are printed in the source, not an OCR artefact. Primary figure recommended for use: 378.221 kg/day (from the dedicated current-status inventory). HCF authorized count of 382 (inventory) vs the gaps narrative on PDF p.68 referencing 578 authorized HCFs and 197 expired/non-renewed - see caveats.

cnd_waste.facility_status: No C&D waste recycling/processing facility exists in the district. 'No facility exist to process C & D waste in the district.' ULBs currently collect C&D waste and dump into low-lying areas; user fee has been fixed. Action plan: identify and develop separate land for C&D processing (timeline 31/08/2022).
cnd_waste.page: PDF p.63 (printed p.62), gaps/action plan PDF p.64-66 (printed p.63-65)
cnd_waste.notes: Confirms the known ~7.2 TPD district total and absence of a C&D recycling facility. District total visually verified as 7.2 (NOT 72 - tesseract dropped the decimal point; the rendered image clearly shows '7.2'). Chikkaballapura CMC specifically = 3 TPD. Per-ULB values sum exactly: 3+2+0.5+1+0.5+0.2 = 7.2 TPD.

extraction_caveats: Source PDF is image-only; all figures obtained by OCR then VISUALLY confirmed on the rendered page image at 250dpi (hazardous PDF p.73, biomedical PDF p.67 and p.69, C&D PDF p.63).
C&D district total: tesseract OCR rendered it as '72' but the page image unambiguously shows '7.2'; per-ULB values sum to exactly 7.2, confirming the decimal. Recorded as 7.2 TPD.

BIOMEDICAL DAILY QUANTITY - INTERNAL DOC INCONSISTENCY (human double-check suggested): the BMW current-status inventory table (PDF p.67 / printed p.66) states 378.221 kg/day generated and treated, while the gaps 'adequacy' table (PDF p.69 / printed p.68) states 378.58 kg/day generated and disposed. Both are printed in the source (not OCR errors) - both visually verified. We recommend 378.221 kg/day as primary (dedicated inventory table); the 378.58 figure is captured as bmw_generated_per_day_alt.

BIOMEDICAL HCF COUNTS - the inventory table gives 225 bedded + 353 non-bedded HCFs and 382 authorized by SPCB. A separate gaps narrative (PDF p.68 / printed p.67) lists a different breakdown summing to 578 authorized HCFs (70 bedded hospitals/nursing homes, 326 clinics/dispensaries, 107 veterinary, 50 pathological labs, 25 AYUSH) and notes 197 had not renewed authorization. The gaps adequacy table (PDF p.69) also uses 578 as 'Existing No of HCE'. The 382 vs 578 difference appears to reflect authorized-this-cycle vs total-on-record categories in the source; not resolved here. Recommended primary figure for 'authorized by SPCB': 382 (inventory table).
Hazardous and C&D figures show no internal inconsistencies; HW sub-totals sum exactly to the stated district total (398.82 MT/Annum) and C&D per-ULB sum exactly to 7.2 TPD.

All quantities are DISTRICT-WIDE except the C&D per-ULB breakdown, which gives Chikkaballapura CMC specifically (3 TPD). Hazardous and biomedical are district-level only; no Chikkaballapura-CMC-specific split is published in the DEP.
